newsitem.title: INDIA: India divestment board report in four weeks - chief.
newsitem.headline: India divestment board report in four weeks - chief.

text.p: A government committee set up to advise on India's divestment programme will finalise its report on some firms in about four weeks, its chairman said on Wednesday.
Disinvestment Commission chairman G.V. Ramakrishna told reporters it hopes to give its recommendations on how to go about divestment in "select few" companies by early March.
The commission was set up in August last year to advise the government on its divestment programme. Forty state-owned firms were referred to the commission.
They included Steel Authority of India, Bharat Heavy Electricals, Mahanagar Telephone Nigam, Air-India and Gas Authority of India.
The commission will decide on the mode of divestment, price and other details based on suggestions from foreign investment bankers and management consultants, he said.
It proposes to ensure that small retail investors are given an opportunity to buy into state-run firms. So far divestments have mostly been through auctioned sales to big institutional investors.
